translations.text: world, as we lived in defilement, drunkenness, revelry, drinking, and impure idol worship, living in malice and envy,
We were hateful, hating one another; we were disobedient, going astray, walking in the emptiness of our heart, darkened in our thoughts;

we were alienated from the life of God because of the ignorance that is in us, because of the hardness of our heart, having given ourselves over to defilement and to the practice of every uncleanness.
But now we were not taught this way. Rather, we were taught: “Work toward your salvation with fear and trembling, for God is the one working in you both to will and to carry out that will.”
For when Moses saw how quick the children of Israel were in those days to forget God's commandments, he ordered them to make tassels on the edges of their garments,
so that they would see them and remember God's commandments and not forget them.
Let us, in turn, place the fear of God in our hearts instead of tassels, so that we do not forget the commandments our fathers handed down to us.
Therefore, brothers, let us turn back and repent before the opportunity slips away from us, and while the light is with us—that is, the teachings of our fathers.
As the Lord said, “Walk while you have the light, so that darkness does not overtake you.” And, “Let us conduct ourselves decently, as in the daytime.”
And, “Those who sleep, sleep at night, and those who get drunk, get drunk at night. But since we belong to the day, let us be sober, having put on the breastplate of faith.”

You share in the suffering of those who are bound, that is, those who are afflicted, as they live on the wild greens of the field because they have found nothing to eat, as you hear. And those who see them testify to their suffering.
Therefore, let us all pray, everyone who fears God, that Christ may keep his blessing enduring in his congregations and not let his places lack anything.
We submit to regulations in the world like people who are alive: “Do not touch, do not taste, and do not go near.”
That is to say, we have come out of the sins of the world and left them behind. Why do we turn back again and wallow in them?
As he also said in this passage: “For you were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord. Live as children of light,
for the fruit of the light consists in all goodness, righteousness, and truth, as you discern what pleases the Lord.
And do not take part in the fruitless works of darkness, but rather expose them.”
For the things they do in secret are shameful even to mention. But all things are revealed when they are exposed by the light, for everything that is revealed is light.
Therefore, let us also rebuke the foolishness within us and all the thoughts the devil casts into us.
and unbelief and hatred, as they make us think evil of one another, even though we are not with one another at all.
And we find fault with one another, and not with ourselves, as though our struggle were against one another and not against the rulers and authorities,
against the world rulers of darkness, against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavens, and not against blood and flesh.
As the apostle said, “Take up the full armor of God, so that you may be able to stand against the devil’s schemes, for our struggle is not against flesh and blood.”
Therefore, keep watch, and let us hold fast to what is good, because there are many who are together in body,
but are far apart from one another in heart and love. There are also many who are not together in body,
yet are always together in the love of Christ, the love of the Spirit, and the will of Jesus.
But you, brothers, be watchful and persevere in the things we have been taught, and many will learn and benefit from you,
just as he said, “Let them see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.”
For just as you have followed all the saints in your conduct, as he said, “But you have followed my teaching, my way of life, my purpose, my faith,
my patience, my love, my endurance, my persecutions, my sufferings”—follow them again by persevering in your own sufferings.
For those who possess the imperishable wealth in Christ are themselves responsible for guarding it for themselves.
If those who possess money, gold, silver, and property
keep watch so that robbers do not steal them, how much more should we keep watch so that the enemy does not steal the good that we do:
our prayers, our fasts, our purity, and our endurance.
For it is not on the same level as the theft of silver and gold. Rather, just as virginity and the monastic life are held in honor,
so too the enemy strives to steal them. Now someone who has acquired pearls or gold stays awake at night to keep watch.
If the enemy stays awake at night to keep watch [?] for the sake of an evil deed, how much more will the person who owns the valuables keep watch so that no one plots against them!
Let us remember what our fathers said: “Brothers who follow our way of life fast and also pray, keeping watch at night,
but they also lie, fight, quarrel, grumble, and slander. They hate, conduct themselves with an estranged heart, and defile themselves,
and they are deceitful, doing every evil deed. People like these toil in vain, and no benefit will come to them. Their endurance, too, is in vain.”
According to what was said: “A sieve does not fill up to produce flour.” And again, in this saying: “Sow wheat, and you will reap thorns.” Their allotted portions will not benefit them.
Therefore, keep watch. Do not let the enemy destroy the good that we do. Rather, guard our heart with every precaution against every impure thought of the devil,
so that we may be worthy to hear this with confidence: “From that time onward they will no longer serve a stranger, but they will serve the Lord their God.”

For robbers do not break into a house or a place where there are no valuables. Rather, they break into the place where they will find valuables. Nor do they break into a place that is being watched, in order to plunder it.
But the places where they know people are not keeping watch and are careless—those are the places they break into, stealing whatever they find.
Likewise, the devil does not rob someone who keeps watch and safeguards the fruits of his labor, but someone whom he finds off guard,
who neither fears God nor considers how he will fall into God's hands,
but drifts with every wind. That is the person from whom he mercilessly snatches away the good he does.
Therefore, brothers and sisters, everyone who is of one heart with God and with our fathers, and also with us, whether male or female, great or small,
With us, and with you also: be humble of heart and keep watch; do not give sleep to our eyes, nor let our eyelids [?] droop [?]
until the Lord rescues us from every temptation of the enemy; for those who envy us are many.
And do not look at brothers who are often agitated by fighting and strife and abandon their endurance, and let them cause you to stumble.
But God will never allow them to cause those who love God to stumble, those whose faith in Christ is complete and who hold fast to the Spirit of God.
But you who sin and abandon your endurance and disturb the congregations through cowardice, envy, and hatred,
and fighting, strife, and deceit—woe to you! What will you do on the day when you are called to account? For your affliction is coming from afar.
Or is it not grounds for condemnation for us, after renouncing what we renounced and binding ourselves by a covenant to the one to whom we bound ourselves, declaring, 'We will not steal,
we will not lie, we will not defile our bodies in any way, we will not bear false witness,
we will not practice any deceit in secret,' together with the other statements that follow these, to turn back again and do these things once more?
Give glory to God! Stand up! I am speaking to you, Aphthonia, daughter of Count Alexander.
Or honor, in your words and deeds, the place where you were brought up, both in the things of God and in the things of the world.
If your heart had not become corrupt, you would not have disgraced the place where you are, or dishonored the brothers and sisters who are there with you.
They call you by the name Aphthonia, yet you envy yourself and begrudge yourself what is good.
You want to destroy your soul, which the whole world is not worth, and to waste all your labor for nothing.
For you have given Satan room to enter you, to change your heart and lead people astray like wandering sheep.
You foolish, ignorant woman, who has no instruction! For if you had understanding, even if they really had fought with you, you ought to let people know what you are like inside your community.
Especially since you told your father and mother, “They fought with me,” or, “They insulted me.” You are lying: they neither fought with you nor insulted you.
Did they fight with you because they corrected you when you broke the commandment and accepted things from your parents without asking?
What did you ask for that you needed, only to have them turn you away or refuse to give it to you? If you tell your father and mother, we are afraid,
especially since you lie. Do you therefore want us to tell them about the foolish things you do, your thefts, and your quarrels?
You truly blind woman, groping at noon like those in the middle of the night, and like blind people who have no eyes!
How, then, will your parents outside in the world hear about your conduct inside this place, while we ourselves in the monastery do not know about it?
If they really mistreated you, oppressed you, or caused you grief, you should have told us about your suffering, so that we could know whether you are telling the truth
or not. Or you should tell your mother who is here with you—if you do not merely call her “Mother” with your mouth,
while your heart is far from her. As it is written, “This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.”
For if your undisciplined heart had not darkened your understanding, would you have despised your fathers who are in the congregation with you?
Or would you have insulted the sisters with whom you live, in your arrogance and contempt for others?
Or if you had not abandoned instruction and wisdom, and loved evil more than good,
would you have rehearsed wicked words and said with your mouth, which is full of cursing and bitterness, “I will go to another monastery”?
How has this place wronged you? Or what burden have they placed on you, except that they told you, “Do not break God’s commandment”?
For you have acted insolently and insulted a girl who lives in the house with you, so that you become a stumbling block and a cause of sin to one another.
For this reason I declare to you: if you do not discipline yourself and rid yourself completely of this disobedience and these quarrels,
I will make your heart suffer, and I will have them deal with you according to what came out of your mouth.

Truly I am distressed about you—or about all of you. I fear that, just as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning, your hearts may be corrupted and led away from the sincerity and purity that lead to Christ.
If he did not leave that woman alone in paradise, will he spare you, or any of you, when you make room for him within yourselves and accept his deceitful schemes and his evil deeds?
For he will not be able to overcome those who fear God, those for whom Christ is a helper and protector.
As it is written: “The one who fights for you is your helper, and he is the sword of your boasting and the glory of your stronghold.”
The person who loves evil is the one who will perish, and he is the one whom the devil will overcome through his soul-murdering deeds.
But the wise person who loves instruction will accept the commandment, and the discerning person who fears the Lord will acquire a guide.
Nevertheless, let me hear that you have put your fathers who are there with you at ease, and obey them in everything, so that our hearts may be at ease, and you yourself may enjoy your peace of mind.
And again, if you have something to say, look: the elders, our fathers and our brothers, have come to you. Tell it to them.
And all of you who have something to say or any matter to raise in your community, do not delay a moment in telling them, and do not hide anything from them.
So that the hearts of all of us together, both us and you, may be at rest, and so that the Lord may also be reconciled to us.
Oh, how careless you are, you who make room for Satan to enter and defile God's holy places, and who defile his temple, which is you yourselves!
Have you not remembered the apostle's declaration: “Whoever defiles God's temple, God will destroy him”?
Nor have you remembered all the curses our father pronounced when he entrusted us all to God, saying: “Cursed is anyone who defiles his body in any way,
or steals any object, from a rope and a belt, especially clothing, a mat, or a hood, down to the smallest item of food,
whether from the property devoted to God's service or from the hands of their neighbors.”
I had intended to come to you in unity of heart. But sorrow over those who angered God and grieved his Holy Spirit prevented our joy.
I know indeed that I deserve every sorrow. But if God and our Lord Jesus are willing, I am coming to you in anger,
to do everything I have in mind to those undisciplined people and those foolish virgins who have no oil in their vessels.
For once again you turn back to those ways of provoking God and fall into the power of the sword of the evil one, who has ruined the whole world through his sins and his lawless deeds,
because you have loved defilement more than purity, and you have chosen death for yourselves rather than life.
For you have provoked the one who created you and nourished you, the eternal God.
And you have also grieved the one who brought you up, Jerusalem, that is, the congregation, and you have fallen at midday like those in the middle of the night.
As it is written: “The virgin of Israel has stumbled and fallen; she will not rise again.”
For he said, “Those who sleep, sleep at night, and those who get drunk, get drunk at night.” But you have become drunk at midday, like those of whom it was said,
“Those who are drunk without wine.” And you have fallen asleep at midday like those who sleep at night, because you have abandoned the fear of God.
You have loved darkness more than light, and you have also regarded what is bitter as sweet and what is sweet as bitter.
Therefore, woe to you wicked people, because you did not remember all the hardship our father endured with all of you. You abandoned his life-giving teachings and the [?] of your fathers.
Nevertheless, look, the elders are coming, and our brothers have come to you again, while we live in great grief and overwhelming sorrow, to deal with each one of you as she deserves.
For you have forsaken the fountain of living water and have dug for yourselves broken cisterns, in that your senseless heart has been darkened.
Saying, “We are wise,” you have become fools, having exchanged the glory of God for unseemly works.
For this reason God handed you over to shameful passions, namely theft, defilement, and every kind of evil.
For these things, every kind of punishment awaits those who do them, not only in this age but also in the other.
